I ported the calculator to Kotlin and it passes all 6 example cases in `node check.mjs`.

The code is in `src/main/kotlin/calc/`, split into three files the same way the Java was: `Parser.kt`, `Main.kt` and `CalcException.kt`. `build.sh` compiles a self-contained jar to `build/calc.jar` and writes `./app`, a small script that runs it with `java`. It uses only the standard library.

I also tried some edge cases by hand, and each matched the spec:
- `(-9223372036854775807 - 1) % -1` prints `0`.
